chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'What do you think if the drinker of nabidh is caught and did not get drunk, will he be flogged with eighty [strikes]?' He said: 'No, and every intoxicant is forbidden.'

key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh (a specific type of fermented drink in early Islamic jurisprudence)
key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: Eighty (referring to the number of lashes)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking nabidh if one does not get drunk?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the fixed hadd of eighty lashes applies specifically to those who become intoxicated, distinguishing it from cases where the drinker remains sober. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the severity of punishment is contingent upon the actual state of intoxication rather than mere consumption, reinforcing the broader Quranic maxim that 'every intoxicant is forbidden.'
